# GitHub Actions security review

## Hand-written CI workflows

`test.yml`, `codspeed.yml`, and `dist-test.yml` set workflow permissions to
`{}`. Jobs that check out source receive only `contents: read`; checkout
credentials are not persisted. The `dist-test.yml` deployment job does not
check out or execute repository code and receives only `id-token: write`.
Deployment requires a successful manual run with `allow_deploy` enabled on
`main`, and publishes the build artifact through PyPI's OIDC trusted publisher.
The PyPI trusted-publisher configuration must identify this workflow and
should be restricted to the `main` ref where supported.

The [pinned CodSpeed v5 action documentation](https://github.com/CodSpeedHQ/action/blob/821a40cd6c80e3cfe387caf55668287addd808da/README.md)
recommends OIDC and its Python example grants `contents: read` and
`id-token: write`; both grants are limited to the benchmark job. The OIDC grant
is job-scoped, so benchmark setup and tests in that job can also request tokens.
Do not treat benchmark execution as isolated from that authority.

`CODECOV_TOKEN` is supplied only to the pinned
[Codecov action](https://github.com/codecov/codecov-action/tree/303a32d7a59b442fa8d48b6a1cc6825c09c847a5),
after tests have completed; it is not an environment variable in the test
process.
GitHub withholds repository secrets from `pull_request` runs originating from
forks, so those uploads do not receive this token. Same-repository pull
requests, pushes to `main`, and authorized manual runs can receive it. The
Codecov action is pinned to a commit, but a same-repository contributor who can
change workflow code is within the trusted boundary for that secret.

| Event | CI token and secret boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Push to `main` | Checkout jobs have read-only `GITHUB_TOKEN`; Codecov gets its upload token; CodSpeed gets the job-scoped OIDC grant. |
| Same-repository pull request | Checkout jobs remain read-only; Codecov gets its upload token; benchmark code runs in the OIDC-enabled job. |
| Fork pull request | Checkout token is read-only and repository secrets are unavailable. CodSpeed still runs with its job-scoped OIDC grant. |
| Manual dispatch | The selected ref is used. The actor must have repository access; configured secrets are available. PyPI publishing is additionally restricted to `main` and `allow_deploy: true`. |
| Comment-triggered automation | None of these three CI workflows is comment-triggered. The separate agentic workflows are reviewed below. |

## Generated agentic workflows

The four `*.lock.yml` files are generated by `gh aw compile`; their Markdown
sources are the corresponding `*.md` files. Their workflow-level permission
baseline is `{}`. `daily-doc-updater` and `weekly-doc-updater` grant read
permissions to their agent jobs. `daily-perf-improver` and
`daily-test-improver` use `read-all` for their agent jobs; this is read-only,
not repository write authority. Their write grants are job-specific:

- Activation jobs can write comments required by command handling; command
  activation is gated by a repository membership check for users with write
  access or higher.
- Safe-output jobs can create the configured issues and pull requests, update
  issues, or push allowed changes to PR branches. Protected paths include
  `.github/`; writes are mediated by the generated safe-output policy.
- The performance and test workflows isolate repo-memory updates in a separate
  `push_repo_memory` job with `contents: write`.
- The weekly documentation workflow's publishing job has `contents: write`,
  `issues: write`, and `pull-requests: write` for its configured PR output.

The generated workflows disable checkout credential persistence. In addition
to the job-scoped `github.token`, generated steps reference separately
configured credentials such as `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`,
`GH_AW_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GH_AW_GITHUB_MCP_SERVER_TOKEN`, and
`GH_AW_CI_TRIGGER_TOKEN`. These credentials are not constrained by YAML
`permissions`; their actual scopes must be verified in repository or
organization settings and kept to the minimum required. Never infer their
scopes from the YAML permission blocks. Fork-origin `pull_request` runs do not
receive repository secrets. Comment-triggered commands are membership-gated;
scheduled and manual runs remain trusted automation entry points.
